title: Five economies where remittance dependence and transfer costs stack up
subtitle: Kyrgyz Republic, Samoa, Tonga, Nepal, and Vanuatu lead a dependence × observed-cost screen—with a four-economy sensitivity core.
finding: After RPW cost-parser repair, the baseline top five by joint remittance dependence and mean corridor cost are Kyrgyz Republic, Samoa, Tonga, Nepal, and Vanuatu; Tonga reaches 42.6% of GDP. The common top-five set across every ±50% sensitivity row is KGZ, TON, VUT, and WSM.
finding_short: Tonga 42.6% of GDP; five-economy baseline with a four-economy sensitivity core.
limits: Triage screen, not a household exposure estimate or country performance ranking.
Nepal is cap-sensitive: under dependence-cap-minus-50, Pakistan enters the top five.
Corridor costs are publicly quoted RPW means; flow-weighted order can change within the same five.
key_messages: High remittance dependence and high observed transfer costs stack in a small set of ADB DMCs.
Repair of the RPW cost parser and flow-weighting keep four economies in every sensitivity top five.
All five baseline economies sit above the SDG 10.c.1 3% cost reference line.

sections.title: Why dependence and cost are read together
sections.body: Remittance dependence alone does not describe household friction. Public corridor prices show whether large flows also face high quoted transfer costs. The screen multiplies those axes only as triage.

sections.title: Repaired baseline
sections.body: After RPW cost normalization repair, the baseline top five are Kyrgyz Republic (26.6% GDP, 10.5% mean cost), Samoa, Tonga (42.6% GDP), Nepal, and Vanuatu. All five mean costs exceed the SDG 10.c.1 3% reference.

sections.title: What stays stable
sections.body: Across the ±50% sensitivity suite the common top-five set is KGZ, TON, VUT, and WSM. Nepal drops only in the dependence-cap-minus-50 row, where Pakistan enters. Median-cost and KNOMAD flow-weighted checks keep the same five economies with reordered ranks.

sections.title: How the screen is built
sections.body: Dependence is WDI personal remittances as percent of GDP. Costs are destination-aggregated RPW corridor quotes with a repaired percent-vs-fraction rule. Flow weighting uses public World Bank/KNOMAD bilateral estimates.

sections.title: What is not claimed
sections.body: The page measures public corridor-cost exposure against macro dependence. It does not estimate household resilience, welfare loss, or policy adequacy.
